pc_new: Secrets found in image and host filesystems via agentless scan
quote: Agentless scanning detects sensitive information inside files in your hosts and container images filesystem.
notes: Detect-secrets page lists checks 424, 425, 597 (Defender, image and container env vars), 456 (image filesystem) and 457 (host filesystem), plus about 50 secret types (AWS, Azure, GCP keys, DB connection strings, SaaS tokens). No S3 bucket scan appears on this page or elsewhere in the 308 Compute pages. Agentless result sends only secret type, file path, line:offset and a short redacted snippet to Console.
ak_onprem_note: The S3 scan runs as a GitHub Actions job that pushes to a configurable accuknox_endpoint (docs/integrations/github-actions-secret-scan.md), so the CI runner must reach the on-prem control plane, and docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AskADA for on-prem.

pc_new: Workload scan and discovery on AWS, with no CSPM module
quote: Prisma Cloud supports agentless scanning of cloud workloads on AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI for vulnerabilities and compliance.
notes: Compute covers AWS workloads: agentless scan of hosts, containers and serverless, cloud discovery of EC2, ECS, EKS, ECR and Lambda, Defenders on ECS, EKS, Fargate, and alert export to AWS Security Hub (not supported for US Gov Cloud regions). CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations is listed as a Compute benchmark (compliance/cis-benchmarks). CSPM is not in Compute Edition per the product-architecture page. Agentless scanners need egress to Console, so a fully air-gapped site cannot use agentless scanning.
ak_onprem_note: Public cloud scanning needs outbound API reach from the on-prem control plane, and docs/resources/deployment.md says on-prem supports all features except AskADA without a per-cloud caveat.

pc_new: Workload scan and discovery on Azure, with no CSPM module
quote: Prisma Cloud supports agentless scanning of cloud workloads on AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI for vulnerabilities and compliance.
notes: Compute covers Azure VMs, AKS, ACI, ACR and Azure Functions through cloud discovery and Defenders. Azure VMs with Trusted Launch enabled are not supported for agentless scanning. CIS AKS Benchmark v1.2.0 is listed. Azure CSPM and org-level posture checks are not in Compute Edition.
ak_onprem_note: Azure scans need outbound API reach from the on-prem control plane, and docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AskADA without an Azure caveat.

pc_new: Workload scan and discovery on GCP, with no CSPM module
quote: Prisma Cloud supports agentless scanning of cloud workloads on AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI for vulnerabilities and compliance.
notes: Compute covers GCP Compute Engine VMs, GKE, GKE Autopilot, Google Artifact Registry and Container Registry, and Cloud Functions. CIS GKE Benchmark covers worker node checks only. Alerts export to Google Cloud SCC. GCP CSPM benchmarks (CIS GCP) are not in Compute Edition. Org-level GCP credentials with hundreds of projects can slow registry discovery, and docs advise splitting by folder.
ak_onprem_note: GCP scans need outbound API reach from the on-prem control plane, and docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AskADA without a GCP caveat.

pc_new: Cloud discovery of VMs, K8s, registries, serverless on AWS, Azure, GCP
quote: Cloud discovery helps you find all cloud-native services being used on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, across all regions, and across all accounts.
notes: Discovery covers registries, serverless functions, managed K8s (ECS, EKS, AKS, ACI, GKE) and VMs, shown in Cloud Radar and Manage > Cloud Accounts. It exists to find unprotected workloads, not to inventory config posture. Auto-defend is not available for Azure VMs and GCP Compute Engine VMs. Alibaba Cloud: cloud discovery is not supported.
ak_onprem_note: Inventory of cloud accounts needs outbound cloud API reach (docs/use-cases/asset-inventory.md), while cluster and VM assets reported by agents work inside the on-prem network per docs/resources/deployment.md.

pc_new: OpenShift 4.12 to 4.22 and Tanzu supported, Nutanix not listed
quote: Prisma Cloud is supported on the following orchestrators.
notes: OpenShift versions in the orchestrator tables range from 4.12 to 4.22 (cri-o). Console install page exists for OpenShift (console-on-openshift). Tanzu: tested hypervisors are VMware Tanzu Kubernetes Grid Multicloud and Integrated, plus Tanzu Application Service Defenders. Nutanix appears only as a PAN VM-Series plugin in the EOL pages, not as a Compute platform. Defenders on Linux VMs would still run on a Nutanix guest OS, but the platform is not named.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md lists OpenShift, OpenStack, VMware, Nutanix and Linux as on-premises sources for the AccuKnox control plane and KubeArmor sensors.

param: Real-Time Automation (e.g., MFA alert on new user)
pc_new: Cloud audit-event alerting sits outside the CWPP-only Compute module
quote: It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: Enterprise Edition claim: audit event policies alert on cloud audit logs. That function sits in the CSPM module, which Compute Edition excludes. Compute alert profiles cover runtime, compliance, vulnerability, cloud discovery and WAAS triggers only. No Compute page mentions CloudTrail ingestion or IAM user events.
ak_onprem_note: CDR ingests cloud logs (docs/use-cases/cdr.md), so an on-prem control plane needs a log path from the cloud accounts, and the docs do not describe CDR on-prem.

pc_new: Compliance for hosts, containers, images and serverless only
quote: Prisma Cloud helps enterprises monitor and enforce compliance for hosts, containers and serverless environments.
notes: Compliance Explorer reports rate per check, rule and regulation with 24 hour trend snapshots. Checks cover Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift, Linux hosts, Windows, Istio and serverless. Manage-compliance page says checks cover images, containers, hosts, clusters and clouds, and the CIS list includes Amazon Web Services Foundations, so some AWS-level checks exist. Multi-cloud posture standards are CSPM and not in Compute Edition.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/compliance.md says air-gapped deployment supports full compliance without external connectivity.

pc_new: Vulnerability, Compliance and Incident Explorers for workloads
quote: Most scanners find and list vulnerabilities, but Vulnerability Explorer takes it a step further by analyzing the data within the context of your environment.
notes: Three explorers: Vulnerability Explorer (per CVE with impacted resources and risk score), Compliance Explorer (rate per check, rule and regulation), Incident Explorer (correlates runtime events into incidents). CSV export on each, SBOM export in CycloneDX 1.4 JSON or XML. Scope is workloads only. No cross-domain dedup with cloud posture findings because CSPM is excluded.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/general.md describes findings deduplication and correlation in the control plane, and docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AskADA for on-prem.

pc_new: Bucket posture checks sit outside the CWPP-only Compute module
quote: It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: Enterprise Edition claim: config policies detect public buckets and alert rules can run CLI auto-remediation. Bucket configuration posture is CSPM scope. Compute pages cover images, hosts, containers, serverless and registries, with no object-storage posture check.
ak_onprem_note: CDR reverts public buckets from CloudTrail events (docs/use-cases/cdr.md), so an on-prem control plane needs a log path and cloud API reach, and the docs do not describe CDR on-prem.

pc_new: Cloud event automation sits outside the CWPP-only Compute module
quote: It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: Enterprise Edition claim was Limited (audit event policies alert only). In Compute Edition no cloud event rule engine exists. Webhook, Jira, Slack and PagerDuty alert profiles fire on workload policy violations, not on cloud account events.
ak_onprem_note: CDR policies run on CloudTrail events (docs/use-cases/cdr.md), so an on-prem control plane needs a log path from the cloud, and the docs do not describe CDR on-prem.

pc_new: Logs all admin changes and logons with user name and source IP
quote: All Prisma Cloud administrative activities are logged.
notes: Settings, rules and credential changes are logged with previous and new values (JSON diff), plus every login attempt and failed API authentication, viewable at Manage > Logs > History by auditor role or higher. Successful API calls are not recorded. App-Embedded runtime, Trust and network firewall audits keep up to 25,000 entries or 50 MB. Syslog and stdout forwarding available. Enterprise Edition claim cited 120 day platform log retention, which does not apply here.
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/audit-trail-logs.md (EventTrail) is a control plane feature, and docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AskADA for on-prem.

pc_new: 8 CIS benchmarks plus PCI DSS, HIPAA, NIST 800-190, GDPR, DISA STIG
quote: To enable the checks for the PCI DSS, HIPAA, NIST SP 800-190, and GDPR standards, select the appropriate template.
notes: CIS list: Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift, Distribution Independent Linux, Amazon Web Services Foundations, GKE (worker nodes only), EKS v1.2.0, AKS v1.2.0. Host scanning adds CIS Amazon Linux 1 and 2. Templates: PCI DSS, HIPAA, NIST SP 800-190, GDPR, DISA STIG (Docker Enterprise 2.x and Kubernetes). Custom checks supported by script. No SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP or CIS Azure/GCP foundations listed. Enterprise Edition claim of 60+ standards does not hold.
ak_onprem_note: docs/support-matrix/compliance-matrix.md lists 42 benchmarks and docs/faqs/compliance.md says air-gapped sites can achieve compliance without external connectivity.

pc_new: Compliance Explorer exports CSV, host scans export PDF or CSV
quote: Report data can be exported to CSV files for further investigation.
notes: Compliance Explorer export honors filters and collections. Host scan compliance (compliance/host-scanning) and VM image compliance (compliance/vm-image-scanning) export PDF or CSV. No scheduled or emailed compliance report is described, unlike the Enterprise Edition claim. No JSON compliance report export is described, but the API returns JSON.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/compliance.md describes PDF, CSV and JSON report export, and docs/resources/deployment.md lists all features except AskADA for on-prem.

pc_new: Jira and ServiceNow tickets, Slack, PagerDuty, email, CSV export
quote: Prisma Cloud can open JIRA issues when new vulnerabilities are detected in your environment.
notes: Alert providers in Compute: email, Jira, ServiceNow (Security Incident Response and Vulnerability Response), Slack, PagerDuty, webhook, Cortex XSOAR and XDR, Splunk, Google Pub/Sub, GCP SCC, AWS Security Hub. Jira routing uses alert labels for project, labels and assignee. Incident Explorer lets you archive incidents. No finding notes, comments, dismiss or snooze with reason appear in the Compute pages, unlike the Enterprise Edition claim.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/general.md lists Jira, ServiceNow, FreshService, ConnectWise and Zendesk, and SaaS ticketing tools such as Zendesk need outbound reach from an on-prem control plane.

pc_new: Native Splunk HEC, syslog to any SIEM, webhooks, Cortex XDR and XSOAR
quote: You can now monitor your Prisma Cloud alerts in Splunk using a native integration.
notes: Splunk uses HTTP Event Collector (Enterprise and Cloud). Console can send syslog directly to a remote endpoint with TLS (audit/logging). Webhook covers anything else. No named Sentinel, QRadar or Sumo Logic integration appears in Compute pages, so those go through syslog or webhook. Enterprise Edition claim of Security Lake, SQS and Service Bus does not apply.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/data-usage-policy.md (not in the nav) says on-prem sends nothing outside unless configured, for example SIEM, and docs/integrations/splunk.md covers Splunk.

pc_new: Alerts create Jira issues and ServiceNow incidents (push only)
quote: New JIRA issues are opened when new vulnerabilities are found.
notes: Jira page describes issue creation per discovery with label-based routing. ServiceNow SIR and VR pages describe field mapping from Prisma Cloud to ServiceNow. No page describes ticket status flowing back to Console. Enterprise Edition claim was also one way. Confirm with Palo Alto Networks if a buyer asks for write-back.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/general.md says AccuKnox marks a finding remediated when the Jira or ServiceNow ticket resolves, which needs the ticket system to call back to the on-prem control plane.

pc_new: Self-hosted Console on any container host, Kubernetes or OpenShift
quote: Compute Console is delivered as a container image, so you can run it on any host with a container runtime (e.g. Docker Engine).
notes: Console install pages exist for onebox (single host, twistlock.sh), Kubernetes, OpenShift, Amazon EKS, AKS, ECS, Fargate, Alibaba ACK, ACS and IBM IKS. Console runs as a Kubernetes Deployment with a persistent volume and a load balancer. Ports 8083 and 8084 inbound. Onebox is described as suited to evaluation.
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/on-prem-installation-guide.md installs the control plane on your own k3s, k0s, OpenShift or RKE2 cluster, and docs/resources/deployment.md says it installs natively on your servers.
ak_new: Self-hosted on VMs or bare metal: k3s, RKE2, OpenShift, EKS, AKS, GKE
ak_evidence: The AccuKnox Control Plane installs natively on your own servers, VMs or bare metal, in your data center.

pc_new: Positioned for air-gapped sites, with manual feed loading
quote: You’re operating in an air-gapped environment.
notes: The page lists air-gapped operation as a reason to pick Compute Edition. Console image ships as .tar.gz in the release tarball and Defender image downloads from Console, and images can sit in your own registry (install/deploy-console/container-images). By default Console reaches intelligence.twistlock.com on 443 and a cloud registry for images, so an offline site must mirror both. Agentless scanning needs scanner egress to Console and cloud APIs, so it does not apply offline.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the air-gapped control plane has no connection to AccuKnox and makes no call-home, but docs/getting-started/on-prem-installation-guide.md lists internet access as mandatory for the 3 VM install, so air-gapped installs use the private registry path.
ak_new: Isolated network with no call-home, images staged in own registry
ak_evidence: The AccuKnox Control Plane runs inside your isolated network and has no connection to AccuKnox.

param: Offline Threat and Vulnerability Feed Updates
pc_new: twistcli downloads the feed and uploads it to an offline Console
quote: Prisma Cloud lets you update Console’s vulnerability and threat data even if it runs in an offline environment.
notes: Basic strategy: download Intelligence Stream data on a connected host (twistcli intelligence download with token), move the archive, upload with twistcli intelligence upload after turning off internet updates. Scale options: serve the feed from an HTTP/S server or a relay Console, and each Console checks every 24 hours. Intelligence Stream is updated several times a day. Projects tenants pull from the Central Console.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/deployment.md says isolated sites must configure automated pipelines to push vulnerability updates, and no step by step procedure appears in the docs.
ak_new: Customer builds the update pipeline, SaaS refreshes every 12 hours
ak_evidence: In isolated deployments, customers must configure automated pipelines to push updates.

pc_new: Data on your Console, anonymous telemetry on by default, can be off
quote: To drive product improvements, Prisma Cloud captures anonymous data about how our product is used.
notes: Telemetry is on by default and is turned off in Manage > System > General. Docs say PAN never collects IP addresses, host names, user names, container labels or image tags. Other outbound paths by default: Intelligence Stream (intelligence.twistlock.com, 443), cloud registry for images, and optional WildFire. Agentless scanners report back to Console. Compute Edition page lists full control over data as a reason to choose it.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says no data goes out on-prem except update pulls, and docs/resources/data-usage-policy.md (not in the nav) still holds an unfilled <ANSWER> placeholder on how updates are fetched.
ak_new: No data egress on-prem, control plane pulls image and chart updates
ak_evidence: No data goes out, and your data never lands at AccuKnox.

pc_new: Projects: one Console per tenant behind a master Console
quote: Projects solve the problem of multi-tenancy.
notes: Each tenant is a supervisor Console with its own Defenders, rules and settings, federated behind one Central Console URL with RBAC per project. A user role applies across all projects. Defenders cannot move between projects. Central and supervisor Consoles must run the same version and talk directly on port 8083 with no proxy. Scale projects are deprecated. Each tenant needs its own Console, so footprint grows per tenant.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/multitenancy.md describes tenant isolation in the control plane with no SaaS-only caveat, and docs/resources/deployment.md says on-prem shares no resources with other customers.
ak_new: Tenants in shared infra with namespaces, or a dedicated control plane
ak_evidence: Each tenant operates in its own K8s namespace.

pc_new: You control upgrades: Console first, then Defenders (n-2 supported)
quote: Deploy the new version of Console first, then manually upgrade all of your deployed Defenders.
notes: Compute docs conflict. This page says Defenders are upgraded manually, while upgrade-helm, upgrade-onebox and upgrade-openshift say Console automatically upgrades deployed Defenders unless auto-upgrade is disabled or fails. App-Embedded Defenders are always manual. Console supports Defenders n, n-1 and n-2 with full support, 31.xx functional, and 30.xx and older disconnect (v34.00). Console upgrade from n-2 must go through n-1. With Projects, all Consoles must run one version.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the customer decides when to upgrade and applies AccuKnox patches with AccuKnox support, but no agent to control plane compatibility window is stated.
ak_new: Customer applies upgrades with AccuKnox support, monthly cadence
ak_evidence: The customer decides when to upgrade.

pc_new: Defenders enforce if Console fails, backup restores to a spare site
quote: When the Console fails or stops working, your environment still has active runtime protection done by the Defenders.
notes: Orchestrator restarts Console against external storage. Clustered-DB mode (configure/clustered-db) syncs 3 to 7 Consoles behind one load balancer across AZs in one region, and needs new Consoles and Defenders. Console takes automatic daily, weekly and monthly backups (DATA_RECOVERY_ENABLED on by default) plus manual backups, restorable from the UI or twistcli. On-prem DR is a warm or cold spare cluster or site restored from backup. Cross-cluster storage replication is not explicitly tested or supported by PAN.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/deployment.md says isolated deployments need customer-configured backup and snapshot procedures, and docs/getting-started/accuknox-arch.md describes multi-AZ control plane HA without an on-prem recipe.
ak_new: Multi-AZ or multi-region control plane, customer-configured backups
ak_evidence: In case of an AZ failure, ingress shifts traffic automatically and pods are rescheduled in remaining AZs

pc_new: x86_64 only, RAM from 512 MB to over 30 GB at 10,000+ Defenders
quote: The Prisma Cloud Console doesn’t support running on ARM64 systems.
notes: RAM tiers from the hardware table: 512 MB minimum without registry scanning, 2 GB with registry scanning, 4 GB with WAAS out of band, 8 GB under 1,000 Defenders, 30 GB for 1,001 to 10,000, over 30 GB above 10,000 (CPU and storage columns scraped ambiguously, so not quoted). Console is a container, so a single Docker host or a Kubernetes cluster works, no full cluster required for onebox. Console does not run on ARM64. Defender needs 256 MB RAM and 8 GB storage. Docker CE 24.0.7 and later, Helm 3.10 and 3.11.
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/on-prem-installation-guide.md and docs/getting-started/on-prem-single-node-installation.md state the requirements, and docs/faqs/deployment.md says an independent Kubernetes cluster is required.
ak_new: Own K8s cluster: 1 node 8 vCPU/32 GB/256 GB, or 3 VMs for POC
ak_evidence: Each node has at least 256 GB of disk space.
